subject: Sing a Song of Sixpence
hook: SING A SONG OF SIXPENCE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The popular claim that 'Sing a Song of Sixpence' was a secret recruitment code for the pirate Blackbeard is a total fabrication, intentionally created by the website Snopes as a 'lost legend' to test people's gullibility.
angle_support: The story that Blackbeard the pirate created 'Sing a Song of Sixpence' with its lyrics as a code to recruit crew for his pirate ship... was created in 1999 by the website Snopes as part of a series of fabricated urban legends.
All the Lost Legends are fictional and the Lost Legend about 'Sing a Song of Sixpence' is no exception.
title: The Pirate Code That Never Existed
description: Discover the true origin of the Blackbeard pirate theory surrounding the classic nursery rhyme. It was never a real code, but a test.
narration: SING A SONG OF SIXPENCE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a hidden pirate code for recruiting crew. You assume these nursery lyrics were actually Blackbeard’s secret signal for planning raids at sea. You believe this because you have heard it everywhere. It was actually closer to a deliberate prank designed to expose your own gullibility. This pirate connection was entirely manufactured in 1999 by the website Snopes. It was part of their 'Repository of Lost Legends' project, cleverly acronymized as TROLL. They created the absurd story to test if people would blindly believe misinformation. Even television producers once fell for the ruse, treating the blatant fiction as a historical fact before being forced to issue a correction. Sometimes the most convincing secrets are just carefully crafted lies waiting for you to believe them.
